_comment: 'EQUIP ALL FREE TO X' MUST BE ONE ENUMERATED ACTION, NOT N EQUIP DIGITS. USER, 2026-10-02, playing KittyEquipment v2 in the play viewer: 'We probably should have a shortcut for equip all to x', '(particularly for free equips)', 'Maybe equip all free to x.' A first cut shipped as a VIEWER MACRO that queued one 'equip=' token per loose piece, and the user came back with 'Equip all free was available, but it only equipped a few.' That was not a viewer bug. A macro can only bundle equips that are IN the menu, and N independent equip digits cannot all be: 14 loose pieces x ~4 hosts is 4^14 against the viewer's 65,536-position plan-space bound, so the valve MUST drop equip groups and no keep policy can make more than ~8 of them survive. The user drew the structural conclusion first -- 'We shouldn't be counting on the unpruned search to fit.' Action::Kind::AttachAllFreeEquipment is the enumeration-side answer: one action per legal host, all of them ONE mutual-exclusion family (bundling everything onto A and then onto B is just 'onto B'), so a product of digits becomes a group of (1 + hosts). This fixture pins the user-visible consequence on the board shape that produced the report: 20 loose Equipment in five four-of classes, metalcraft live via Puresteel Paladin so every equip is {0}, and two legal hosts. 'equipallfree=0' is the any-host wildcard, so a 'choose' with two variants is the assertion that BOTH hosts are offered -- the enchant_target dedup collapse (one bundle action per host, every one carrying the host's name as its card_name, so with no sub-decision they share a signature and all but the first vanish) measured as accept/1-variant before the sub was added. MTG_UNPRUNED rides alongside MTG_HUMAN_PLAY because the viewer always sets both; without it the autonomous group cap drops the bundle's group along with the equips.
